I am a PhD student preparing a survey presentation on recent advances in natural language processing, specifically focusing on large language models and their reasoning capabilities. I need to gather information from multiple sources, organize it systematically, and create both a data spreadsheet and a presentation.

First, visit the survey methodology guide at http://localhost:30231 to learn about how to structure a literature survey. The main page explains the overall approach including comparison criteria and taxonomy development. There is also a guide page at http://localhost:30231/guide.html with tips on presenting survey results effectively. Take notes on the recommended structure and presentation tips.

Next, search the arxiv paper database for recent papers related to NLP, language models, and reasoning. You should find around five relevant papers on these topics. For each paper, look up its full details including the abstract and read its LaTeX source to extract the key methodology, the datasets used in experiments, and the main findings. The LaTeX source of each paper (its section headings and content) is available through the arxiv-latex tools (list_paper_sections, get_paper_section, get_paper_prompt). In the content returned by these tools, each section heading appears on its own line starting with '#', so you can count the sections of a paper by counting those heading lines (or by reading the sections list returned by list_paper_sections). Count the LaTeX sections of each paper, because the survey needs the average number of sections across papers.

After gathering all the paper information, create an Excel workbook called Survey_Data.xlsx in the workspace with three sheets. The first sheet should be named "Paper Comparison" with columns Paper_ID, Title, Year, Method, Dataset, and Key_Finding. The Paper_ID column must contain each paper's arXiv identifier in the standard form YYMM.NNNNN (for example 2404.00001), with no prefix such as "arXiv:" and no version suffix such as "v1". The Method column should describe the core approach in a few words, the Dataset column should list the primary evaluation dataset, and Key_Finding should summarize the main result. The second sheet should be named "Taxonomy" with columns Category and Papers. Group the papers into meaningful categories based on their approaches such as prompting methods, training methods, and architectural innovations. The third sheet should be named "Summary Statistics" with columns Metric and Value, including Total_Papers, Most_Common_Category, Year_Range, and Average_Sections (average number of LaTeX sections across papers). All values in the Value column must be written as literal text or numbers in the cell itself — do NOT write Excel formulas (for example, do not enter "=COUNTA(...)" or "=AVERAGE(...)"; instead write the plain number, e.g. 5 or 4.0).

Then create a PowerPoint presentation called NLP_Survey.pptx in the workspace. The presentation should have at least six slides. The first slide should be a title slide with a title containing the words "NLP Survey" or "Language Model Survey" or similar. The second slide should present the survey methodology and structure based on what you learned from the methodology guide. Then include one slide for each of at least three key papers, showing the paper title, its method, dataset, and key finding. End with a summary slide that provides a taxonomy overview and identifies key trends across the surveyed papers.

Please review the survey outline and presentation style guide files in the workspace for additional context about the expected structure and formatting guidelines.

Important coordination note: this is a multi-agent task and all agents share the same workspace. Each of the two final files (Survey_Data.xlsx and NLP_Survey.pptx) must be written to disk by a single sub-agent. Never have more than one agent write the same file at the same time — concurrent writes to the same file overwrite each other. Coordinate your work so that, after the research information has been gathered, one designated sub-agent is responsible for writing Survey_Data.xlsx and one (or the same agent) is responsible for writing NLP_Survey.pptx.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, follow this exact orchestration plan. A wave must finish and return all stated handoffs before the next wave begins. Within a wave, dispatch exactly one sub-agent for each numbered sub-task and run those sub-agents concurrently.

Before Wave 1, the main agent must list and read all task-visible survey-outline and presentation-style reference files in read-only mode, without assuming their filenames, and freeze the survey comparison schema, taxonomy/statistics rules, at-least-six-slide contract, and single-writer ownership of Survey_Data.xlsx and NLP_Survey.pptx. It must resolve the task-visible workspace directory from the runtime allowed-directory listing (or literal accessible-workspace directory already supplied by the harness), freeze `<workspace_root>`, and reject bare `/workspace` and dumps/run-specific paths. It must then inspect the granted runtime tool catalog and verify that the task-required LaTeX section operations can actually read section lists and contents for discovered paper IDs. If those operations are unavailable or no authorized source can return the required paper bodies, the main agent must stop before delegation, report the exact missing-capability blocker, and must not fabricate Method, Dataset, Key_Finding, section counts, or either dependent deliverable. The following waves apply only when the required source capability is present; all paper facts must come from task-visible runtime sources.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 2 sub-agents in parallel, one for each numbered sub-task:

   1. explore 0 (web-domain-researcher 0): Use one explore sub-agent to inspect both task-provided survey-methodology pages in read-only mode and combine their source-backed guidance with the frozen local-reference packet supplied by the main agent. Use only the granted non-interactive browser navigation, snapshot, search, and wait operations; do not click, type, evaluate scripts, select options, invoke terminal, or reread workspace files. Return a compact source-referenced methodology packet covering comparison criteria, taxonomy guidance, recommended presentation structure, slide tips, and per-page/reference coverage. Do not write deliverables or alter the pages.

   2. explore 1 (academic-literature-researcher 0): Use one explore sub-agent to scout the task-relevant local arXiv candidate space read-only for recent NLP, language-model, and reasoning papers. Use complementary queries at the supported per-call result bound, union and deduplicate by stable ID because no search cursor is exposed, validate relevance from title/abstract, and return a candidate manifest with authors/date, abstract, available arxiv-latex status, per-query/union controls, and rejected distractors. Do not read full manuscripts, write files, or create deliverables.

After Wave 1, the main agent must apply the task's relevance rule, select exactly five source-supported papers, and freeze an explicit five-row assignment table containing `agent_no`, stable ID, and exact title, with one distinct paper per row.

Before dispatching Wave 2, render each numbered prompt into a complete self-contained instruction that includes that row's literal stable ID and exact title, the permitted read-only paper/LaTeX calls, the complete return schema and all missing/conflict controls. Never send an agent only an ordinal such as "paper row 3" or require it to infer fields from another prompt.

2. Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 5 explore sub-agents in parallel, one for each frozen paper:

   1. explore 0 (academic-literature-researcher 1): Use one explore sub-agent to own only paper row 1 from the frozen assignment table.
   2. explore 1 (academic-literature-researcher 2): Use one explore sub-agent to own only paper row 2 from the frozen assignment table.
   3. explore 2 (academic-literature-researcher 3): Use one explore sub-agent to own only paper row 3 from the frozen assignment table.
   4. explore 3 (academic-literature-researcher 4): Use one explore sub-agent to own only paper row 4 from the frozen assignment table.
   5. explore 4 (academic-literature-researcher 5): Use one explore sub-agent to own only paper row 5 from the frozen assignment table.

Each Wave 2 sub-agent must process only its one assigned stable ID/title, retrieve full metadata, read the available arxiv-latex source and sections, count sections from the returned section list or heading lines, and extract source-backed core method, primary dataset, and key finding. Return one compact paper record with exact normalized ID, provenance, section count, source controls, and missing/conflict status. Explore is read-only, so do not write files or create Excel or PowerPoint.

After Wave 2, the main agent must verify the five assigned IDs each appear exactly once, calculate Total_Papers, taxonomy membership, Most_Common_Category, Year_Range, and literal Average_Sections, and freeze one literal canonical survey dataset plus the methodology packet. Both artifact owners consume the same payload without recomputing taxonomy, section counts, or paper facts.

3. Wave 3 — dispatch exactly 2 sub-agents in parallel, one for each numbered sub-task:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Use one coder sub-agent to own `<workspace_root>/Survey_Data.xlsx` exclusively. Use one `python_execute` with `openpyxl` to create Paper Comparison, Taxonomy, and Summary Statistics atomically from the canonical payload with exact headers, standard IDs without prefix/version, literal Value cells, source-backed method/dataset/finding rows, and verified taxonomy/statistics. Then read each complete populated range once and return path, sheet order, row/metric controls, and validation. Do not write the presentation.

   2. coder 1 (office-report-builder 1): Use one coder sub-agent to own `<workspace_root>/NLP_Survey.pptx` exclusively. Use one `python_execute` with `python-pptx` to create the complete deck atomically from the canonical payload, with at least six slides including a title slide, methodology slide grounded in the webpage/guide packet, at least three distinct paper slides, and a final taxonomy/trends summary. Follow the visible style guide, then read the deck once and return path, slide count/titles, paper/methodology coverage, and validation. Do not write the workbook.

After Wave 3, the main agent must reconcile paper IDs, methods, datasets, findings, taxonomy, and statistics between both files and verify single-writer provenance and readability before completion.

You are a read-only web researcher helping prepare a PhD survey presentation on LLM reasoning. Your job is to read the survey methodology guide hosted on a local website and report its contents in a structured form.

Tasks:
1. Navigate to http://localhost:30231 — the main page of a "survey methodology guide". It explains the overall approach to structuring a literature survey, including comparison criteria and taxonomy development.
2. Navigate to http://localhost:30231/guide.html — a companion guide page with tips on presenting survey results effectively.
3. Capture ALL substantive text from both pages (verbatim quotes of key lists are welcome). Specifically note:
   - The recommended survey structure (steps/phases)
   - Comparison criteria for comparing papers
   - Taxonomy development guidance
   - Presentation tips / recommendations for communicating survey results
4. If the pages link to other relevant pages on the same host (e.g., about methodology details), briefly visit and capture them too, but stay within http://localhost:30231.

Deliverable: a complete report containing (a) main page content summary with all named comparison criteria and structure steps, (b) guide.html presentation tips verbatim or near-verbatim, (c) any other useful details found. This report will be used directly to build an Excel summary and PowerPoint slides, so completeness matters more than brevity.
Read survey methodology website

You are a read-only academic literature researcher. I am building a survey presentation on recent advances in natural language processing, focusing on large language models (LLMs) and their reasoning capabilities (chain-of-thought prompting, reasoning benchmarks, training methods like RLHF/instruction tuning, architectural innovations, etc.).

Your job: select EXACTLY 5 arXiv papers and extract structured metadata for each, using the available arxiv tools:
- mcp__arxiv_local__search_papers / mcp__arxiv_local__list_papers / mcp__arxiv_local__read_paper (a local mirror of arXiv; list_papers first to see what's already available locally)
- mcp__arxiv-latex__get_paper_abstract, mcp__arxiv-latex__list_paper_sections, mcp__arxiv-latex__get_paper_section, mcp__arxiv-latex__get_paper_prompt

Workflow:
1. First call mcp__arxiv_local__list_papers to see which papers are locally available. If ~5 suitable papers on NLP / language models / reasoning topics are available locally, prefer those. Otherwise use mcp__arxiv_local__search_papers with queries like '"large language model" AND reasoning', '"chain-of-thought"', 'reasoning language models' in categories ["cs.CL", "cs.LG", "cs.AI"], and download/select 5 relevant papers.
2. Selection guidance: prefer papers relevant to LLM reasoning, covering a MIX of approaches if possible (prompting methods like chain-of-thought/tree-of-thought, training methods like RLHF/instruction tuning/RLVR, architectural innovations, evaluation/benchmarks). Papers should ideally be from 2022 or later.
3. For EACH of the 5 selected papers, gather:
   a. Exact arXiv ID in the canonical form YYMM.NNNNN (e.g., 2404.00001). CRITICAL: report the bare ID only — NO "arXiv:" prefix and NO version suffix like "v1"/"v2". If the source gives "arXiv:2201.11903v6", report "2201.11903".
   b. Full title.
   c. Year (from the arXiv ID: first two digits are year-of-month YY, e.g., 2201 → 2022, 2303 → 2023). Verify by abstract text if needed.
   d. Abstract (get_paper_abstract).
   e. The LaTeX section count: call mcp__arxiv-latex__list_paper_sections to get the list of sections, and/or mcp__arxiv-latex__get_paper_prompt (the flattened LaTeX) and count lines that are section headings starting with '#'. Report the count of section headings as "Sections_Count". If list_paper_sections returns a list, its length is the count. If the two disagree, report list_paper_sections length.
   f. Core METHOD (the paper's approach in a short phrase, e.g., "chain-of-thought prompting with few-shot examples", "RLHF fine-tuning").
   g. Primary DATASET(S) used in experiments (e.g., GSM8K, MMLU, HumanEval). Read the experiments/method sections via get_paper_section or read_paper to find them; do NOT guess.
   h. KEY FINDING: one sentence summarizing the main result (preferably with numbers from the abstract/results section).

Deliverable: a structured report with, for each of the 5 papers:
- Paper_ID (bare YYMM.NNNNN), Title, Year, Sections_Count, Method (short phrase), Dataset (primary evaluation dataset(s)), Key_Finding (one sentence), plus a 3-5 sentence methods summary from the LaTeX source.

Also suggest a tentative taxonomy grouping: which papers are "prompting methods", which are "training methods", which are "architectural innovations" or "evaluation/benchmarks", since the survey will group papers that way.

Completeness and accuracy of IDs, section counts, datasets, and findings matter most — this feeds directly into an Excel workbook.
Research 5 arXiv LLM papers

You are a report-builder sub-agent in a shared multi-agent workspace. Your SOLE file-writing responsibility: create /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_Qwen3.8-Max/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-survey-presentation/workspace/Survey_Data.xlsx. Do NOT create, modify, or touch any other deliverable (another agent owns NLP_Survey.pptx and is writing it concurrently — leave it alone).

All data is provided below — do not search, fetch, or re-derive anything. Just build the workbook exactly as specified.

Use mcp__local__python_execute with openpyxl to create the file. Requirements:

Workbook: Survey_Data.xlsx with exactly 3 sheets, in this order:

SHEET 1: "Paper Comparison"
Row 1 headers: Paper_ID | Title | Year | Method | Dataset | Key_Finding
Data rows (exactly these 5, in this order):
1. Paper_ID: 2404.00001 | Title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting for Complex Reasoning | Year: 2024 | Method: Few-shot chain-of-thought prompting with 4-8 step-by-step reasoning demonstrations | Dataset: GSM8K, MATH | Key_Finding: CoT prompting improves accuracy by 15% on GSM8K and 12% on MATH over standard prompting
2. Paper_ID: 2404.00002 | Title: Instruction Tuning for Improved Language Understanding | Year: 2024 | Method: Instruction tuning on 50K curated instruction-response pairs with LoRA (rank 64) fine-tuning | Dataset: MMLU, BBH, TriviaQA | Key_Finding: 10B model reaches 72.5% on MMLU, outperforming 5x larger models; instruction quality and diversity matter more than quantity
3. Paper_ID: 2404.00003 | Title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP | Year: 2024 | Method: RAG combining Contriever dense retrieval (top-5 passages) with a fine-tuned LLaMA generator | Dataset: Natural Questions, TriviaQA | Key_Finding: Reduces hallucination by 40% on knowledge-intensive tasks while improving factual accuracy
4. Paper_ID: 2404.00004 | Title: Self-Consistency in Language Model Reasoning | Year: 2024 | Method: Self-consistency decoding sampling 40 chain-of-thought paths and marginalizing to the most frequent answer | Dataset: GSM8K, SVAMP, AQuA | Key_Finding: Improves chain-of-thought accuracy by 8% on GSM8K without any additional training
5. Paper_ID: 2404.00005 | Title: Multimodal Large Language Models for Visual Reasoning | Year: 2024 | Method: CLIP vision encoder fused with LLaMA via projection layer, trained with visual instruction tuning on 600K image-text pairs | Dataset: VQA v2, GQA, VizWiz | Key_Finding: State-of-the-art results on VQA v2, visual dialogue, and COCO captioning
CRITICAL: Paper_ID cells must be stored as TEXT strings (set number_format='@' / quote-prefix so Excel keeps "2404.00001" verbatim — never as a number, never with an "arXiv:" prefix or version suffix like v1).

SHEET 2: "Taxonomy"
Row 1 headers: Category | Papers
Rows:
- Prompting Methods | 2404.00001, 2404.00004
- Training Methods | 2404.00002
- Architectural Innovations | 2404.00003, 2404.00005

SHEET 3: "Summary Statistics"
Row 1 headers: Metric | Value
Rows (all Value cells as literal text/numbers — absolutely NO Excel formulas, nothing starting with '='):
- Total_Papers | 5 (numeric)
- Most_Common_Category | Prompting and Architecture (tied, 2 each)
- Year_Range | 2024
- Average_Sections | 4.0 (numeric)

Formatting: bold header rows; reasonable column widths; freeze top row optional.

Verification (must be done before you finish): reopen the saved file with openpyxl (data_only=False) and print every sheet's name and every cell's value + type + number_format; confirm (a) sheet names exactly match, (b) Paper_ID cells are strings equal to '2404.00001'...'2404.00005', (c) no cell value starts with '=', (d) Total_Papers==5, Average_Sections==4.0.

Deliverable to return: confirmation the file exists at the exact path, plus a dump of the verification output.
Build Survey_Data.xlsx workbook

You are a report-builder sub-agent in a shared multi-agent workspace. Your SOLE file-writing responsibility: create /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_Qwen3.8-Max/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-survey-presentation/workspace/NLP_Survey.pptx. Do NOT create, modify, or touch any other deliverable (another agent owns Survey_Data.xlsx and is writing it concurrently — leave it alone).

All content is provided below — do not search, fetch, or re-derive anything. Build an 9-slide deck with the mcp__pptx tools (create_presentation, add_slide, manage_text, populate_placeholder, add_table, save_presentation). Style per the conference guidelines: concise bullet points (no long paragraphs), clear takeaways per slide, consistent look, comparison table included.

SLIDE 1 — Title slide:
Title: "NLP Survey: Recent Advances in Language Model Reasoning"
Subtitle: "Large language models, prompting, training, and architecture — a systematic survey"

SLIDE 2 — "Survey Methodology & Structure":
- Goal: systematically organize recent LLM reasoning research to identify trends, gaps, and future directions — structured analysis, not just a paper list
- Research questions: How has LLM reasoning improved? Which approaches dominate — prompting, training, or architecture? Which benchmarks are used?
- Comparison criteria (consistent framework): methodology type, evaluation benchmarks, dataset size, model scale, improvement over baselines
- Taxonomy: papers grouped by primary approach (prompting / training / architecture) — mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive
- Paper selection: 5 recent papers (2024) from arXiv covering NLP, language models, and reasoning

SLIDES 3–7 — one slide per paper. Each slide's title contains the paper title and its ID; body bullets labeled Method / Dataset / Key Finding:
SLIDE 3 "Chain-of-Thought Prompting for Complex Reasoning (2404.00001)":
- Method: Few-shot chain-of-thought prompting with 4-8 step-by-step reasoning demonstrations
- Dataset: GSM8K, MATH
- Key Finding: +15% accuracy on GSM8K and +12% on MATH over standard prompting; longer chains help complex problems
SLIDE 4 "Instruction Tuning for Improved Language Understanding (2404.00002)":
- Method: Instruction tuning on 50K curated instruction-response pairs; LoRA rank-64 fine-tuning
- Dataset: MMLU, BBH, TriviaQA
- Key Finding: 10B model reaches 72.5% on MMLU — beats 5x larger models; instruction quality and diversity beat quantity
SLIDE 5 "Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP (2404.00003)":
- Method: RAG combining Contriever dense retrieval (top-5 passages) with a fine-tuned LLaMA generator
- Dataset: Natural Questions, TriviaQA
- Key Finding: 40% reduction of hallucination on knowledge-intensive tasks with better factual accuracy
SLIDE 6 "Self-Consistency in Language Model Reasoning (2404.00004)":
- Method: Self-consistency decoding — sample 40 CoT reasoning paths via temperature sampling, marginalize to the most frequent answer
- Dataset: GSM8K, SVAMP, AQuA
- Key Finding: +8% over chain-of-thought on GSM8K with zero additional training
SLIDE 7 "Multimodal Large Language Models for Visual Reasoning (2404.00005)":
- Method: CLIP vision encoder + LLaMA via projection layer; visual instruction tuning on 600K image-text pairs
- Dataset: VQA v2, GQA, VizWiz
- Key Finding: State-of-the-art on VQA v2, visual dialogue, and COCO captioning

SLIDE 8 — "Paper Comparison" with a comparison table (use add_table). Columns: Paper_ID | Method | Dataset | Key Finding. Fill with:
- 2404.00001 | Few-shot CoT prompting | GSM8K, MATH | +15% GSM8K, +12% MATH
- 2404.00002 | Instruction tuning + LoRA | MMLU, BBH, TriviaQA | 72.5% MMLU with 10B model
- 2404.00003 | RAG (Contriever + LLaMA) | NQ, TriviaQA | -40% hallucination
- 2404.00004 | Self-consistency decoding | GSM8K, SVAMP, AQuA | +8% over CoT, no training
- 2404.00005 | Multimodal LLM + visual instruct. tuning | VQA v2, GQA, VizWiz | SOTA on VQA v2

SLIDE 9 — "Summary: Taxonomy & Key Trends":
Taxonomy overview (structured list with counts):
- Prompting Methods — 2 papers: 2404.00001 (CoT), 2404.00004 (Self-Consistency)
- Training Methods — 1 paper: 2404.00002 (Instruction Tuning)
- Architectural Innovations — 2 papers: 2404.00003 (RAG), 2404.00005 (Multimodal)
Key trends:
- Training-free inference-time techniques (CoT, self-consistency) deliver large, cheap gains
- Instruction quality and diversity beat data quantity; smaller well-tuned models rival much larger ones
- Grounding — retrieval and vision — is the main route to factual and multimodal reasoning
- GSM8K is the de-facto standard reasoning benchmark
Open questions (future work):
- How does reasoning scale beyond math to general tasks?
- How to measure reliability/hallucination rigorously?
- How to combine retrieval + multimodal evidence inside reasoning chains?

Steps: create a new presentation, add the 9 slides (title layout for slide 1), fill all text/table content, then save_presentation to the exact path above. Finally call extract_presentation_text on your presentation and return: (a) confirmation of the saved file path, (b) the full extracted text so the coordinator can verify slide titles and content.
